title.narrative: START Fund 909 South Sudan (Displacement due to conflict)

description.narrative:
The crisis in Magwi County, South Sudan, began on January 18, 2025, when herders from Jonglei State relocated to Ayii and Nyolo, causing extensive crop destruction and displacement of the host community. This move was driven by unresolved tensions from a 2022 cattle raid and ongoing livestock destruction of crops. Suspected armed youth from the Greater Pibor Administrative Area allegedly raided cattle from the Jonglei herders, who suspected local authorities and the community of colluding with the raiders due to the lack of recovery of stolen cattle. The herders brought an estimated 8,000 to 10,000 cattle into Ayii and Nyolo, resulting in the destruction of nearly 100 hectares of farmland. The host community rejected the herders’ pledge to compensate for the damage and demanded their immediate departure. Negotiation efforts failed, and on January 31, 2025, armed youths from the Pibor Administrative Area attacked cattle camps in Ayii and Nyolo, leading to 41 reported deaths, widespread burning, and looting.
On February 1, 2025, reports emerged of destruction and looting in Agoro Centre, including the vandalization of youth and women’s centres supported by UNHCR. In response, the host community, mainly women and children, fled toward Magwi Centre, Obama, Obo, Pajok, and Iwonkibook. The attackers are believed to have fled eastward with the stolen livestock, but their exact destination remains unclear. The primary challenge is the fluid and tense security situation, which restricted movement in and out of affected areas, hindering humanitarian agencies from conducting on-the-ground assessments at the time. However, with coordinated engagement and advocacy including participation of UNMISS to support to escort and facilitate access, Interagency Needs Assessment finally took place on the 5 Febuary 2025 that informed the raising of alert and subquent activation of alert 909.
"Success will mean that the affected communities can adapt and transition towards early recovery and resilience. Cash assistance and shelter support will play a critical role in meeting the diverse needs of displaced households, including access to food, medicine, and emergency shelter. By providing multi-purpose cash assistance (MPCA), families will have the flexibility to prioritize their most urgent needs, restoring dignity and agency in decision-making. Shelter assistance will ensure safe and dignified living conditions, reducing exposure to protection risks and improving resilience. These interventions will also create enabling conditions for return, allowing households to resume agricultural activities, plant crops, and successfully transition through the lean season until the next harvest.
